claims.statement: UDT states that public-road-transport charging stations and charging points are subject to its technical examinations for safe operation, repair and modernization.
UDT states that examination fees are tied to the prior-year average wage and paid after the examination or opinion, creating a concrete statutory paid event.
A model-specific preflight product may reduce correction cycles and revenue delay, but UDT does not publish enough rejection data here to establish the size of that saving.
Current first-pass failure rates and average days lost to documentation corrections are unknown.

contrary_evidence: UDT publishes forms and guidance, while charger manufacturers and competent installers may already deliver complete packs.
The statutory examination fee belongs to UDT and is not addressable revenue; only incremental preparation value is capturable.
Low inspection failure rates would collapse the value proposition.

economics.acquisition_route: Sell through charger distributors, installers, OCPP back-end providers and commercial-property electricians; the family renewables channel can identify local installers and host sites.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A labelled database of requested corrections, negative findings, charger models, site configurations and remedial actions can make preflight checks increasingly specific.
fingerprint.customer: Polish charge-point operators, property owners and EV-charger installers preparing public stations or returning stations to service after repair or modernization.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Sell through charger distributors, installers, OCPP back-end providers and commercial-property electricians; the family renewables channel can identify local installers and host sites.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A model-specific document linter, remote commissioning checklist, annotated evidence vault and licensed-electrician review that produces a UDT submission pack and tracks requested corrections. Charge per connector or site without promising approval or preferential scheduling.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The operator pays the statutory UDT examination fee after the examination and would pay a fixed preflight fee per site for a submission-ready pack. The UDT fee is evidenced; the private preflight budget and value of avoided delay require validation.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Before operation, or after a repair or modernization that triggers an operational examination, the owner must assemble technical documentation, pass an on-site UDT examination and avoid a negative decision that delays charging revenue.

founder_fit: Directly adjacent to renewable installation and electrical workflows.
Document intelligence and checklist automation are cheap to prototype.
Per-site work can be channel-led and later expanded into fleet compliance software.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: UDT preflight and commissioning evidence for public EV chargers
uncertainties: How many new, repaired or modernized public sites per year are accessible through small and mid-sized installers?
Which documentation defects are machine-checkable versus dependent on an on-site licensed judgment?
Professional-liability and insurance requirements for a paid preflight opinion.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Obtain 50 anonymized historical submission packs and outcomes from at least 10 installers, build a blind defect checklist and measure whether it predicts every correction without false assurances. Offer five paid preflights with a refund of the service fee if a document defect within the declared scope is missed.
